title: Thailand Hospital Bed Capacity
thesis: Snowflake turns daily ward-level capacity data from a synthetic Thai private hospital group into occupancy, admissions and boarding KPIs, 7-day capacity overflow risk scores, boarding-time anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables, with no patient records.

talking_points: Bed occupancy, admissions vs plan, admissions placed outside the placement target and confirmed capacity overflows for 40 wards across 5 Thai cities.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to ward-day rows.
The pressure-driver chart shows which bed-management escalations turn into confirmed overflows and which are mostly cleared on review.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of bed capacity KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which wards should the bed management team look at first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each ward for the probability of a confirmed capacity overflow in the next 7 days. It is an operational bed-flow score, not a diagnostic or clinical prediction.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags boarding-time outliers per ward, and the forecast projects daily admissions for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: Bed-flow audit compliance, equipment safety-check coverage and average boarding time, from the curated tables.
The scatter compares audit compliance with confirmed overflows by ward; it is a synthetic association, not evidence of cause.
The action memo is drafted by an LLM from the KPI, ward, pressure-driver and risk rows only, and needs human review.
tabs.call_out: From numbers to a reviewed action plan

transition.line: What is happening on the wards right now?

talking_points: Live bed-census events arrive from the native simulator (Snowflake only) or Firehose, S3 and Snowpipe (AWS build).
Events carry no patient identifiers: ward, wait for a bed, boarding hours and status.
The alert logs ALERT events with an SOP hint and emails the bed management team.
tabs.call_out: Live ward signals with an alert and email

transition.line: Can we ask the data directly?

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers metric questions through the semantic view and cites bed-flow SOPs from Cortex Search.
Each answer shows the SQL it ran, so the figures can be checked.
Try: which 3 wards have the most confirmed capacity overflows, and what SOP applies?
tabs.call_out: Grounded answers with SQL and SOP citations

talking_points: Both builds are shown, the current one first: Snowflake only, and AWS + Snowflake with Firehose, Bedrock and QuickSight.
Every flow in the diagrams is built by the scripts in the repository.
Alerts and tasks stay suspended between demos.
tabs.call_out: One platform for data, ML, AI and the app
